name: human and organisational
reason: The people and process lens now has a domain. Twelve of its Class I factors are covered by review procedures that produce evidence, and the twenty seven Class III factors stay unavailable because they are internal governance facts. Nothing here is observed: no social engineering test plan exists.

L11-026.note: Reporting practice covers how to communicate a finding. Disclosure handling as a process is named only by adjacency.

L11-030.note: The same class of mistake recurring, measured per team.

L11-009.note: A login from a leaver's account after the last day is the evidence.

L11-010.note: One credential used from several distinct clients is the attribution failure.

L11-011.note: A live secret in a non manager store, with its location, is the finding.

L11-014.note: A device without an enrollment record holding data is the unmanaged trust case.

L11-015.note: Work data present on a device outside management is the boundary test.

L11-019.note: An elevated session with no approval record is the trail question.

L11-027.note: A report marked out of scope for a real issue is the scope defect.

L11-028.note: The safe harbour statement read for what it actually protects.

L11-031.note: A sensitive change merged with one approval and no security review.

L11-032.note: A sensitive file with no named owner.

L11-039.note: A key used by several distinct clients is the sharing symptom.

L11-055.note: What the organisation says it will never ask for, checked against its real process.

L11-002.note: A reset completed by a single actor without a second approval, from the audit record.

L11-008.note: An initial password visible to a third party in transit.

L11-037.note: A support view exposing fields unrelated to the request.

L11-025.note: Time from report to a human acknowledgement, including out of hours.

L11-013.note: Third party hosting terms are read from the vendor, which is the same review path as the MFA entry.
